long_biography.plain_text:
Nikkie Plessen approached Kate Moss by email to collaborate on her fashion business. A meeting in London led to the model becoming the face of the label and selecting a collection of favourite pieces. Plessen also uses her own public profile to market the clothes, wearing them in daily posts for her followers.

The discipline behind that visibility developed in television. At music channel TMF, she prepared interviews, selected news and wrote presentation cards before the afternoon broadcast. Her design work has included staff uniforms for restaurants: black dresses for De Librije in Zwolle and clothing for The Jane in Antwerp.

confidence.reason: Her direct business interview supplies the approach, marketing practice and television duties; independent fashion reporting documents the selected collection and restaurant commissions.

uncertainties: Identity is supported by exact name, full birth date, Dutch background, official link to the source Instagram and matching partner. A direct independent Jolie X ownership declaration was not required to manufacture confidence and no vessel facts enter either biography.
Forbes-first queries included site:forbes.com/profile Nikkie Plessen and exact-name Forbes follow-ups. No verified personal Forbes profile was found.

Source Instagram is corroborated by official backlink and her direct interview. Existing LinkedIn is preserved, but direct retrieval returned 999 and no independent official backlink was found. No duplicate rows are proposed.

Searches covered Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitter/X, YouTube, TikTok and personal website. Official Facebook backlink resolves to a person/brand channel but its page body could not be inspected to distinguish personal from corporate use, so withheld. A historic Twitter handle lacks current strong verification. YouTube lifestyle channels and guest videos are corporate or third-party. The old nikkieplessen.nl site was unavailable and not proposed.

Family business guidance supports the advantaged-start interpretation, but no source establishes that she received Ruben's prior business assets or a principal family capital transfer. Her personally earned television experience is not itself treated as inherited advantage.

Capital A acquired control after a large partial sale. The exact retained stake, investment of sale proceeds and personal asset balance remain undisclosed; the current fashion classification has reduced confidence. No majority ownership by Plessen is asserted.
Sources differ between 2011 activity and 2012 launch, and between counts of items in the first collection. The prose omits those particulars.
The source Mrs honorific is retained without treating it as proof of marriage. Missing middle names, additional nationality and secondary residence remain unsupported.

Apparel retail, Fashion designer and Television presenter satisfy distinct industry/profession dimensions. No manufacturing tag is inferred from outsourced production, no cosmetics specialism from one brand name, and no model tag from promoting her own clothes. Acting remains documented in prose without another overlapping screen-career tag. No formal taxonomy candidates created.
